meta.provenance: Authored from model knowledge (cutoff Jan 2026). Original explanations - not copied from Adobe documentation. Shortcuts/menu paths are factual data.
meta.iconNote: Adobe icon artwork is proprietary; app renders software chip fallback.

commands.name: Selection Tool
commands.description: Selects, moves and scales whole objects and groups with a bounding box. The default resting tool when assembling plan graphics and diagram elements on an artboard.

commands.name: Direct Selection Tool
commands.description: Selects individual anchor points, handles and path segments inside objects and groups. Essential for tweaking a traced site boundary or nudging one corner of a plan outline.

commands.name: Group Selection Tool
commands.description: Selects one object within a group, then progressively larger parent groups with further clicks. Useful for picking a single tree symbol out of a heavily grouped landscape plan.

commands.name: Magic Wand Tool
commands.description: Selects all objects sharing an attribute such as fill colour or stroke weight in one click. Brilliant for grabbing every wall poche or every red annotation across a busy drawing at once.

commands.name: Lasso Tool
commands.description: Selects objects and anchor points by dragging a freehand loop around them. Quick for gathering a scatter of points or small elements that a rectangular drag would miss.

commands.name: Pen Tool
commands.description: Draws precise paths from anchor points and bezier handles. The fundamental Illustrator skill for tracing site plans, drawing bespoke symbols and constructing clean diagram geometry.

commands.name: Add Anchor Point Tool
commands.description: Adds an anchor point wherever you click on an existing path. Used when a straight boundary needs a new kink or a curve needs an extra control point.

commands.name: Delete Anchor Point Tool
commands.description: Removes the anchor point you click, letting the path re-flow through its neighbours. Handy for cleaning up over-noded paths produced by Image Trace or CAD imports.

commands.name: Anchor Point Tool
commands.description: Converts anchors between sharp corners and smooth curves, and adjusts handles independently. The tool for turning a boxy traced outline into flowing landscape curves, or vice versa.

commands.name: Curvature Tool
commands.description: Draws smooth curves by simply placing points, with corners on a double-click. A friendlier route than the Pen for sweeping masterplan paths, roads and organic diagram lines.

commands.name: Type Tool
commands.description: Creates point text with a click or area text with a drag. Everything from board titles to plan labels and key notes starts here.

commands.name: Type on a Path Tool
commands.description: Flows text along any drawn path. Used for labelling curved roads and rivers on masterplans, or running a title around a circular diagram.

commands.name: Line Segment Tool
commands.description: Draws individual straight lines; hold Shift for exact horizontals, verticals and 45-degree angles. The staple for leader lines, section markers and hatching bases in diagrams.

commands.name: Rectangle Tool
commands.description: Draws rectangles and squares as live shapes with editable corner radii. The starting point for room blocks, bar-chart diagrams and panel frames on portfolio layouts.

commands.name: Rounded Rectangle Tool
commands.description: Draws rectangles with pre-rounded corners; the arrow keys adjust the radius while dragging. Useful for soft-edged diagram cards and button-like labels in presentation graphics.

commands.name: Ellipse Tool
commands.description: Draws ellipses and, with Shift, perfect circles. Constantly used for bubble diagrams, tree canopies in plan and circulation nodes.

commands.name: Polygon Tool
commands.description: Draws regular polygons, with arrow keys changing the number of sides mid-drag. Reached for when a hexagonal grid or triangular annotation marker is needed.

commands.name: Star Tool
commands.description: Draws stars with adjustable point counts and radii. Occasionally useful for map markers, ratings graphics or decorative diagram accents.

commands.name: Paintbrush Tool
commands.description: Draws paths that carry a brush stroke, from calligraphic nibs to art brushes. Used to give diagram linework a hand-drawn warmth or apply textured edges to plan graphics.

commands.name: Pencil Tool
commands.description: Draws freehand paths that follow your drag, with adjustable smoothing. Good for loose concept-sketch linework over a plan without the formality of the Pen.

commands.name: Smooth Tool
commands.description: Drag along a wobbly path to relax it and remove excess anchor points. The quick fix for jittery hand-traced contours and sketchy diagram lines.

commands.name: Blob Brush Tool
commands.description: Paints strokes that become filled, merged shapes rather than stroked paths. Ideal for chunky freehand poche, shadow blocks and marker-style diagram fills.

commands.name: Eraser Tool
commands.description: Rubs away vector artwork, cutting and reshaping the underlying paths. Useful for carving openings out of filled diagram shapes without Pathfinder gymnastics.

commands.name: Scissors Tool
commands.description: Cuts a path at the point you click, leaving open ends. Used to break a plan outline so one segment can take a different lineweight or dashed style.

commands.name: Knife Tool
commands.description: Slices through filled objects along a freehand or straight drag, producing closed shapes on both sides. Handy for splitting a site plan area into phased zones.

commands.name: Rotate Tool
commands.description: Rotates the selection around a movable reference point; Alt-click sets the point and opens the dialogue for exact angles and copies. Rotating copies around a centre is the classic way to array seats or trees around a focal space.

commands.name: Reflect Tool
commands.description: Mirrors the selection across an axis through a chosen reference point, optionally as a copy. Perfect for symmetrical plan elements - draw half a facade diagram and mirror the rest.

commands.name: Scale Tool
commands.description: Resizes the selection about a reference point, with a dialogue for exact percentages and the choice of scaling strokes too. Useful for rescaling drawing content to a new metric scale while controlling lineweight behaviour.

commands.name: Shear Tool
commands.description: Skews the selection along an axis around a reference point. Used to fake quick axonometric projections of plan shapes for exploded diagrams.

commands.name: Free Transform Tool
commands.description: Combines scale, rotate, distort and perspective distortion in one widget. Reached for when an image or graphic must be pushed into a rough perspective on a board.

commands.name: Width Tool
commands.description: Varies a stroke's width along its length by dragging at any point. Gives plan and section linework calligraphic emphasis, thickening cut lines and tapering leader ends.

commands.name: Shape Builder Tool
commands.description: Merges or subtracts overlapping shapes by simply dragging across the regions you want, or Alt-dragging to delete. The intuitive alternative to Pathfinder for composing plan poche and diagram geometry.

commands.name: Live Paint Bucket Tool
commands.description: Fills any enclosed region formed by overlapping paths, treating linework like a colouring book. Excellent for colouring imported CAD plans where rooms are bounded but not closed shapes.

commands.name: Mesh Tool
commands.description: Adds a gradient mesh to a shape so colour can be blended freely across its surface. An advanced technique for soft site-plan shading or painterly sky panels in vector.

commands.name: Gradient Tool
commands.description: Applies and adjusts linear, radial and freeform gradients directly on the object. Used for graded diagram fills, subtle depth on plan figures and sky bands in vector visuals.

commands.name: Eyedropper Tool
commands.description: Samples and applies complete appearance attributes - fill, stroke, type styling - from one object to another. The fastest way to make a new element match the drawing's established graphic language.

commands.name: Blend Tool
commands.description: Generates intermediate steps between two or more objects, blending shape and colour. Useful for contour-like transitions, arrayed steps along a path and smooth colour ramps in diagrams.

commands.name: Symbol Sprayer Tool
commands.description: Sprays instances of a symbol across the artboard, with companion tools to shift, size and tint them. An efficient way to scatter trees or people symbols over a masterplan while keeping the file light.

commands.name: Artboard Tool
commands.description: Creates, resizes and rearranges artboards within the document. Used to set up a suite of board sizes or one artboard per diagram for tidy multi-page export.

commands.name: Hand Tool
commands.description: Pans around the canvas; hold the spacebar to borrow it from any tool. Second nature when working across a large masterplan at high zoom.

commands.name: Zoom Tool
commands.description: Zooms the view in with a click or scrubby drag, and out with Alt held. Constantly used to swing between whole-board composition and anchor-level path editing.

commands.name: Rotate View Tool
commands.description: Tilts the canvas view without rotating the artwork itself. Comfortable for drawing along an angled street grid or annotating a rotated site plan.

commands.name: Toggle Fill and Stroke
commands.description: Switches whether the fill or the stroke swatch is active for editing. A tiny key press that prevents endlessly recolouring the wrong attribute.

commands.name: Swap Fill and Stroke
commands.description: Exchanges the current fill and stroke colours on the selection. Quick when flipping between outlined and solid versions of diagram elements.

commands.name: Default Fill and Stroke
commands.description: Resets the selection to a white fill with a black stroke. A clean starting state before styling new construction lines or test shapes.

commands.name: None (No Fill or Stroke)
commands.description: Sets the active fill or stroke attribute to none. Used constantly to strip fills from boundary lines or strokes from colour blocks in plan graphics.

commands.name: Join
commands.description: Connects the endpoints of open paths, closing gaps with a straight segment or fusing coincident ends. Constantly needed to close boundaries in imported CAD linework before filling.

commands.name: Average
commands.description: Moves selected anchor points onto a shared horizontal, vertical or central position. Paired with Join to snap two loose line ends exactly on top of each other before fusing them.

commands.name: Outline Stroke
commands.description: Converts a stroked line into a filled closed shape of the same visible width. Essential before booleans on lineweights, and for freezing stroke widths ahead of scaling or laser-cutting exports.

commands.name: Offset Path
commands.description: Creates a new path a set distance inside or outside the original. Directly useful for wall thicknesses, setback lines and concentric diagram rings at exact spacings.

commands.name: Simplify
commands.description: Reduces the number of anchor points on a path while preserving its shape as closely as possible. The remedy for bloated paths from Image Trace or GIS and CAD imports.

commands.name: Add Anchor Points
commands.description: Inserts a new anchor point midway along every selected segment. Useful before distortions or scripts that need denser geometry to work with.

commands.name: Divide Objects Below
commands.description: Uses the selected path as a cookie cutter to slice everything beneath it. A quick way to cut a masterplan graphic along a phase line or site boundary.

commands.name: Make Compound Path
commands.description: Combines paths so overlapping areas become holes, like the counter of a letter O. How you punch courtyard voids through a building footprint while keeping it one object.

commands.name: Pathfinder Panel
commands.description: Hosts the boolean shape operations: unite, subtract, intersect, exclude and the divider modes. The engine room for constructing plan poche and diagram geometry from overlapping primitives.

commands.name: Pathfinder: Unite
commands.description: Merges the selected shapes into one combined outline. Used to fuse overlapping room blocks into a single building footprint.

commands.name: Pathfinder: Minus Front
commands.description: Subtracts the front shape from the one behind it. The standard move for cutting openings, courtyards and notches out of plan shapes.

commands.name: Pathfinder: Intersect
commands.description: Keeps only the area where the selected shapes overlap. Handy for trimming a hatch or colour field precisely to a site boundary.

commands.name: Pathfinder: Divide
commands.description: Slices all selected shapes into separate faces along every overlap. Useful for splitting a plan into individually colourable zones defined by crossing boundary lines.

commands.name: Group
commands.description: Binds the selected objects so they select and transform as one. Grouping each tree symbol, each key entry and each diagram element keeps complex plans manageable.

commands.name: Ungroup
commands.description: Releases the selected group back into independent objects. Often applied repeatedly to dismantle deeply nested imports from CAD or PDF.

commands.name: Lock Selection
commands.description: Locks the selected objects so they cannot be selected or moved. Lock the base plan underlay before drawing over it and nothing shifts by accident.

commands.name: Unlock All
commands.description: Unlocks every locked object in the document. The counterpart to habitual locking when it is finally time to move the underlay.

commands.name: Hide Selection
commands.description: Hides the selected objects from view and selection. Useful for temporarily clearing annotation clutter while composing the underlying drawing.

commands.name: Show All
commands.description: Reveals every hidden object again. Worth pressing before export - hidden elements are easy to forget entirely.

commands.name: Bring to Front
commands.description: Moves the selection above everything else in its layer. Keeps labels and leader lines reading clearly over dense plan graphics.

commands.name: Bring Forward
commands.description: Raises the selection one step in the stacking order. For fine-tuning which diagram element overlaps which.

commands.name: Send Backward
commands.description: Lowers the selection one step in the stacking order. Used when a colour block should sit just beneath its outline but above the base map.

commands.name: Send to Back
commands.description: Drops the selection beneath everything else in its layer. Typically applied to background tints and base-map imagery.

commands.name: Align Panel
commands.description: Aligns and distributes selected objects relative to each other, a key object or the artboard. Indispensable for regimenting legends, image grids and repeated diagram frames.

commands.name: Transform Again
commands.description: Repeats the last move, rotation, scale or reflection, including its copy option. Move-copy once then hammer Ctrl+D to array fence posts, grid lines or parking bays at perfect spacing.

commands.name: Transform Each
commands.description: Transforms every selected object around its own centre rather than a shared one, with optional random variation. Perfect for resizing or jittering a field of tree symbols so they stop looking stamped.

commands.name: Move (Transform)
commands.description: Opens a dialogue for numeric movement by exact distance and angle, with a copy option. The precise way to shift drawing elements a known site dimension, scaled to the drawing.

commands.name: Paste in Front
commands.description: Pastes the clipboard at its exact original position, directly in front of the selection. Vital for stacking duplicate boundaries in perfect registration, such as a clipping copy over its source.

commands.name: Paste in Back
commands.description: Pastes the clipboard at its original position but behind the selection. Useful for slipping a tint or halo shape exactly beneath existing linework.

commands.name: Paste in Place
commands.description: Pastes at the same coordinates as the source, including across documents. Keeps registration when moving drawing content between board files sharing an artboard size.

commands.name: Isolation Mode
commands.description: Double-click a group to edit its contents alone while everything else dims and locks. The sanest way to adjust one element inside a densely grouped masterplan.

commands.name: Swatches Panel
commands.description: Stores fills, strokes, gradients and patterns for reuse, including global swatches that update every use when edited. Define your plan palette as global colours and a whole drawing recolours in one edit.

commands.name: Recolour Artwork
commands.description: Remaps every colour in the selection through a single dialogue, with harmonies and reduction options. Transforms a whole diagram to a new palette in minutes - ideal for matching office brand colours or testing schemes.

commands.name: Transparency Panel
commands.description: Controls opacity and blend modes, and creates opacity masks for gradual fades. Multiply here is the everyday mode for layering colour zones over base plans without hiding linework.

commands.name: Appearance Panel
commands.description: Lists and edits every fill, stroke and effect stacked on the selected object, in order. Lets one path carry a double lineweight or a casing-and-centreline road style without duplicate geometry.

commands.name: Stroke Panel
commands.description: Controls stroke weight, caps, corners, dashes and arrowheads. Where drawing conventions live: dashed setback lines, section arrows and consistent lineweight hierarchies.

commands.name: Graphic Styles Panel
commands.description: Saves complete appearance recipes that can be applied to any object with one click. Build styles for cut walls, glazing and vegetation once, then keep every drawing in the set consistent.

commands.name: Create Outlines
commands.description: Converts live text into vector shapes, freezing it against font substitution. Standard practice before sending board files to print bureaus or cutting text on a laser - keep an editable copy first.

commands.name: Character Panel
commands.description: Sets typeface, size, leading, tracking and other character attributes. The control centre for a coherent typographic hierarchy across labels, titles and key notes.

commands.name: Paragraph Panel
commands.description: Controls alignment, justification, indents and spacing for paragraphs. Used to keep blocks of narrative text and long key lists tidy on presentation boards.

commands.name: Area Type
commands.description: Flows text inside any closed shape, created by clicking a path with the Type Tool. Lets project descriptions wrap neatly within irregular panel shapes on a board layout.

commands.name: Layers Panel
commands.description: Organises artwork into layers and sublayers with visibility, locking and selection controls. Structure masterplans like CAD - base, buildings, landscape, annotation - and navigation stays painless.

commands.name: New Layer
commands.description: Adds a fresh layer to the document from the Layers Panel. Give each drawing system its own named, coloured layer before the file grows unwieldy.

commands.name: Make Clipping Mask
commands.description: Uses the topmost shape to crop everything selected beneath it, non-destructively. The standard way to trim a map, hatch or image neatly to a site boundary or board frame.

commands.name: Release Clipping Mask
commands.description: Undoes a clipping mask, restoring the full extent of the clipped artwork. Needed when the crop boundary itself has to be redrawn or the hidden content retrieved.

commands.name: Cycle Drawing Modes
commands.description: Switches between Draw Normal, Draw Behind and Draw Inside modes. Draw Inside clips new strokes to a shape as you draw - useful for hatching directly within a plan zone.

commands.name: Symbols Panel
commands.description: Stores reusable artwork as symbols whose instances all update when the master is edited. Define a tree or person symbol once and revise hundreds of placements across a masterplan in one go.

commands.name: Make Pattern
commands.description: Turns selected artwork into a repeating pattern swatch, with live preview of tiling options. Purpose-built for creating hatch fills - paving, planting, brick - that tile cleanly across plan areas.

commands.name: Image Trace
commands.description: Converts placed raster images into editable vector paths, with presets from line art to full colour. Useful for vectorising scanned hand sketches or logos; expect a clean-up pass with Simplify afterwards.

commands.name: Expand
commands.description: Converts live effects, symbols, strokes or traced results into plain editable paths. The necessary step before hand-editing Image Trace output or sending artwork to cutting machines.

commands.name: Effect: Drop Shadow
commands.description: Adds a live, editable shadow behind objects via the Appearance stack. A restrained drop shadow lifts building footprints off a site plan and gives figure-ground diagrams gentle depth.

commands.name: Effect: 3D and Materials
commands.description: Extrudes, revolves or inflates flat artwork into rendered 3D with lighting and materials. Quick for turning a plan shape into a simple massing axonometric without opening a modelling package.

commands.name: Effect: Transform
commands.description: Applies a live, editable transform - including multiple copies - as an effect. Elegant for parametric-feeling arrays: one balustrade module becomes fifty, all still driven by the original.

commands.name: Apply Last Effect
commands.description: Re-applies the most recent effect with identical settings to the current selection. Keeps a family of diagram objects visually consistent without reopening dialogues.

commands.name: Rasterise
commands.description: Converts vector artwork into a pixel image at a chosen resolution inside the document. Sometimes needed to tame files where heavy effects or meshes slow every redraw.

commands.name: Artboards Panel
commands.description: Lists, reorders, renames and duplicates the document's artboards. Naming artboards properly pays off at export, when files inherit those names automatically.

commands.name: Export for Screens
commands.description: Batch-exports artboards or assets to PNG, JPEG, SVG or PDF at multiple scales in one pass. The fastest route from a multi-artboard diagram file to a complete set of named deliverables.

commands.name: Asset Export Panel
commands.description: Collects dragged-in artwork as named assets for repeated one-click export. Ideal for icon sets and diagram elements that get re-exported every time they are tweaked.

commands.name: Save As
commands.description: Saves the document under a new name or format, including PDF with editing capability retained. Saving as PDF straight from Illustrator is the usual route for issuing review sets of boards.

commands.name: Export As
commands.description: Exports to formats such as PNG, JPEG, TIFF, SVG or DWG, optionally per artboard. The DWG option is a handy bridge when vector diagram work needs to travel back into CAD.

commands.name: Place
commands.description: Imports images, PDFs or other files, either linked to the source or embedded. Linked placement keeps board files light and lets an updated render flow through automatically.

commands.name: Document Setup
commands.description: Edits document-wide settings including units, bleed and transparency options. Where you confirm millimetres and add printer's bleed before boards go anywhere near a print bureau.

commands.name: Package
commands.description: Gathers the document with all linked images and fonts into one folder for handover. The safe way to pass a board file to a colleague or printer without missing-link surprises.

commands.name: Outline Mode
commands.description: Toggles a wireframe view showing bare paths without fills, strokes or effects. Invaluable for finding stray points, hidden duplicates and unclosed boundaries in a complex plan file.

commands.name: Preview on CPU
commands.description: Toggles between GPU-accelerated and CPU rendering of the canvas. Worth switching when GPU preview shows hairline artefacts on dense linework or the display misbehaves.

commands.name: Pixel Preview
commands.description: Previews artwork as it will rasterise, revealing anti-aliased edges at pixel level. Check diagrams destined for screens or web portfolios here before exporting fuzzy linework.

commands.name: Smart Guides
commands.description: Toggles the dynamic magenta alignment hints that snap to edges, centres and angles while you draw and move. Keep them on for diagram assembly; switch off when they fight a dense drawing.

commands.name: Rulers
commands.description: Toggles rulers along the window edges, the source for dragged guides. First stop when setting up margins and a grid for a portfolio board.

commands.name: Hide Guides
commands.description: Toggles guide visibility without deleting them. Flick guides away to judge the board composition, then bring them back to continue aligning.

commands.name: Make Guides
commands.description: Converts any selected path into a non-printing guide. Powerful for setting up angled or curved construction guides that match a site geometry, not just verticals and horizontals.

commands.name: Release Guides
commands.description: Turns guides back into ordinary editable paths. Useful when a construction guide should become real drawn geometry after all.

commands.name: Lock Guides
commands.description: Locks all guides so they cannot be nudged while drawing. Sensible default once a board grid is set, sparing you mysteriously drifting margins.

commands.name: Show Grid
commands.description: Displays the document grid behind the artwork. A useful armature for modular diagram layouts and consistent spacing across a board set.

commands.name: Snap to Grid
commands.description: Makes drawing and moving operations snap to the document grid. Turn it on for strictly modular diagrams; leave it off for freeform plan tracing.

commands.name: Snap to Point
commands.description: Snaps dragged objects onto nearby anchor points and guides. The accuracy habit that keeps plan linework genuinely connected rather than nearly touching.

commands.name: Fit Artboard in Window
commands.description: Zooms so the current artboard fills the window. The reflex reset after detailed path editing deep inside a board.

commands.name: Fit All in Window
commands.description: Zooms out until every artboard is visible at once. The overview shot when juggling a document that holds a whole set of presentation boards.

commands.name: Actual Size
commands.description: Shows the artwork at 100 percent, which Illustrator maps to real-world print size on most displays. A useful sanity check that lineweights and type will read at the board's true scale.

commands.name: Hide Edges
commands.description: Hides the coloured selection highlights on paths while keeping the selection active. Lets you judge a colour or lineweight tweak without glowing anchor clutter in the way.

commands.name: Hide Bounding Box
commands.description: Hides the transform bounding box around selections. Helpful when the handles keep inviting accidental scaling during delicate plan editing.

commands.name: Undo
commands.description: Steps back through recent edits, with a deep history. The safety net that makes experimental diagram styling cheap.

commands.name: Redo
commands.description: Reinstates edits you have just undone. Handy for toggling a change on and off to compare versions of a graphic decision.

commands.name: Select All
commands.description: Selects every unlocked object in the document, or all text when in a text frame. Usual first step before a global transform or a document-wide recolour.

commands.name: Deselect
commands.description: Clears the current selection. Worth the habit before checking the drawing, since selection highlights can mask true colours and weights.

commands.name: Select Same Fill Colour
commands.description: Selects every object in the document sharing the current fill colour; siblings cover stroke colour, weight and more. The menu counterpart to the Magic Wand for sweeping graphic clean-ups.

commands.name: Preferences
commands.description: Opens application settings including units, keyboard increment and scaling behaviour. Setting units to millimetres and a sensible arrow-key nudge distance makes drawing work far less fiddly.
